findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct item 3 / Scope: compact.py's `_git` does NOT raise CommandError from cp.stderr (it emits a fixed 'Error: git operation failed while holding lock' and discards stderr), so either add a per-site change to surface the augmented exhaustion stderr through compact.py or drop compact from the 'no per-site changes' list.
evidence: Plan quote: 'the returned CompletedProcess.stderr is augmented with the lock file path ... so every existing call site (txn/compact/delete raise CommandError from stderr) surfaces one actionable error with no per-site changes.'
compact.py:59 `_git` returns `run_git_write(tracker, *args, check=False)` (no raise, no stderr surfacing).

compact.py:377-379 and 385-387 handle a non-zero returncode by `sys.stderr.write("Error: git operation failed while holding lock\n")` then `return 1` — a FIXED string; a whole-file search for `.stderr` in compact.py returns no matches, so cp.stderr is never surfaced.

Contrast: txn.py:131 raises `CommandError(f"Error: git operation failed: {cp.stderr}", ...)` and delete.py:182 raises `CommandError(f"...during delete: {cp.stderr.strip()}", ...)` — both DO carry the augmented stderr, so the plan's claim holds for txn/delete but NOT compact.
findings.finding: Item 3's premise that 'every existing call site (txn/compact/delete raise CommandError from stderr) surfaces one actionable error with no per-site changes' is refuted for compact.py: its `_git` failure paths discard `cp.stderr` and emit a fixed generic message, so the augmented exhaustion stderr never reaches the operator without a per-site change.
findings.location: Approach item 3 ('One actionable exhaustion error'); src/rebar/_commands/compact.py (_git at line 59; failure branches at lines 378 and 386)
scenarios: A permanently held index.lock/ref-lock exhausts the retry budget during `rebar compact`: the operator sees only 'Error: git operation failed while holding lock' with no lock-file path or holder guidance, so the AC's 'one actionable error naming the contended lock file' is not met on the compact path.
findings.suggested_fix: Add compact.py to the touched-files scope and change its git-failure branches (compact.py:378, :386) to include `cp.stderr` in the emitted message, mirroring txn.py:131 / delete.py:182, so the run_git_write exhaustion guidance reaches the operator.

evidence: fsck.py:387 `def _git(*args): return run_git(tracker, *args, check=False)` — a closure INSIDE `_tracker_sync_status`, not a module-level wrapper
fsck.py:357-361 `cp = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", tracker, "symbolic-ref", ...], capture_output=True, text=True)` inside `_branch_mismatch` — a second, unwrapped, unbounded read-only git call
Plan speaks of a single `fsck.py's read-only _git` wrapper receiving the 120s fold
findings.finding: AC5 asserts the local-only git sites are covered 'by reading the five touched wrappers' and Approach item 5 names 'fsck.py's read-only _git', but fsck.py has TWO read-only git call sites: the named `_git` is a nested closure inside `_tracker_sync_status` (calls run_git), while `_branch_mismatch` issues a separate DIRECT `subprocess.run` git invocation with no bound and no wrapper — this second site is neither named nor bounded by the plan.
findings.location: Approach item 5 / AC line 5 ('checked by reading the five touched wrappers') / Scope (src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py)
scenarios: fsck run against a wedged filesystem hangs in `_branch_mismatch`'s symbolic-ref call, which the plan's watchdog never covers
AC5's 'five touched wrappers' check misses the second fsck git site, so the AC can be marked done while a site stays unbounded
findings.suggested_fix: Route `_branch_mismatch`'s `subprocess.run` through the same bounded wrapper (or state its deliberate unbounded rationale) and update Approach item 5 to reflect fsck's two read-only git sites.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the seam mismatch: either route event_append's _git_add/_git_commit/_git_rm through run_git_write, or explicitly extend the advisory lock + watchdog to event_append._run_git (and add it to Scope), so the append/batch write path is actually covered by advisory serialization — the Testing 'appending through the seam' bullet currently exercises a wrapper the append path does not use.
evidence: event_append.py routes its 13 lock-held git calls through its OWN _run_git (`run_git_write` has zero matches in event_append.py); _git_add/_git_commit/_git_rm all call _run_git
Plan: 'All changes at the store's local git execution seam so every routed call site inherits them' — but the append seam is a different wrapper
Testing: 'two concurrent processes appending through the seam both succeed (advisory serialization)' — the append seam bypasses run_git_write
ticket comment (c2ba closure): 'event_append.py routes all 13 lock-held git calls through a new _run_git() bounded by _GIT_TIMEOUT=30' — a separate wrapper from run_git_write
Scope lists gitutil.py/lock.py/fsck.py/metrics but NOT event_append._run_git
findings.finding: The advisory lock (Approach item 1) and 120s watchdog (item 5) are added only to run_git_write, but the highest-frequency write path — event_append.stage_and_commit / batch_stage_and_commit and the UU/invalid-object recovery — routes through event_append._run_git, not run_git_write. So the 'advisory serialization' the Testing section tests ('two concurrent processes appending through the seam both succeed') and the operator decision cite does not cover the append/batch path.
scenarios: Two concurrent agents both appending events (the normal high-concurrency mode) contend on index.lock but never take the advisory lock, because their add/commit go through event_append._run_git
The plan's advisory-serialization test either fails, or is written against run_git_write and gives false confidence that the append path is serialized

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the 300s watchdog surfaces in git_metrics._git given its check=True / .stdout-returning contract (it cannot be 'exactly like event_append._run_git' which is check=False): e.g. drop check=True and have callers treat rc!=0 as unavailable, or catch TimeoutExpired and return an Unavailable/None — and confirm blame.py's all-exception swallow already covers its fold.
evidence: git_metrics.py:20-28 `_git` runs subprocess.run(..., check=True) and returns .stdout
No CalledProcessError handling in git_metrics.py (search: CalledProcessError -> no matches)
event_append._run_git uses check=False and folds timeout into CompletedProcess(argv,124,...) for a returncode-inspecting caller
Plan: '300s (research 5b rec 3) ... folded into a synthetic rc-124 result exactly like event_append._run_git'
findings.finding: The plan says metrics/git_metrics.py gets a '300s watchdog, folded into a synthetic rc-124 result exactly like event_append._run_git', but git_metrics._git uses check=True and returns .stdout directly, with no CalledProcessError/returncode handling anywhere in the module. A synthetic rc-124 CompletedProcess does not compose with check=True and returning .stdout — the mechanism copied from event_append (which is check=False and returns the result for a returncode-inspecting caller) does not fit here.
scenarios: git blame/log walk exceeds 300s: the 'rc-124 fold' produces a CompletedProcess the check=True caller never inspects; churn()/callers read .stdout and get an empty/garbage result instead of a clear failure
typecheck/behavior differs from the event_append precedent the plan cites as identical

findings.location: Scope: "src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py — bound its local `_git` wrapper (120s, rc-124 fold)"; Approach item 5: "`fsck.py`'s read-only `_git` gets the same 120s fold"
scenarios: fsck.py `_branch_mismatch`'s inline `git symbolic-ref` subprocess.run stays unbounded after the plan lands — a wedged filesystem/lock during that call hangs fsck with no rc-124 watchdog, violating the AC that each local-only git site in Context be bounded or documented as deliberately unbounded
The AC checked by 'reading the five touched wrappers' passes for fsck.py's `_git` while silently leaving a second git call site in the same listed file uncovered

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider adding git's three core.*Timeout knobs (core.filesRefLockTimeout / packedRefsTimeout / configLockTimeout, Gitaly precedent) to the store git invocations because they absorb ref/config-lock contention inside git at zero uncontended cost and compose with the advisory lock — or state explicitly why the operator-ratified advisory-lock+retry supersedes this fully-cited rec (which the research ranks highest-value).
evidence: Research rec 5b#1: 'SET GIT'S THREE LOCK KNOBS ON EVERY INVOCATION — highest value per unit risk, and the only fully cited-precedent move (Gitaly)'
Research 'IF YOU ARE DESIGNING ON TOP OF THIS': 'REDUCE THE CONTENDED SURFACE RATHER THAN CONTEND BETTER'
ticket status comment: 'Remaining research recs not yet done: #2 core.*Timeout knobs, #3 retry jitter, #4 watchdog...' — plan folds in #3/#4 but not #2 knobs
Plan AC: 'the chosen approach cites them rather than asserting a value' — but the core.*Timeout-knob rec is neither adopted nor rejected-with-reason
findings.finding: The research recorded on this ticket names two higher-value, fully-cited contention reducers (set git's three core.*Timeout knobs on every invocation — Gitaly precedent, rec 5b#1/#3; and GIT_INDEX_FILE isolation for the append path, rec 5b#9/footgun 8) that reduce the contended surface rather than contend better. The plan adopts neither and does not state why the operator-ratified advisory-lock+retry supersedes the cheaper core.*Timeout knobs, which compose with (rather than replace) the chosen approach.
scenarios: HEAD.lock/packed-refs.lock/config.lock contention under agent storms: git's own retry (with the knobs set) would absorb it inside git at zero cost, whereas the plan re-implements ref-lock retry in Python (item 2) and leaves config.lock unaddressed
A reviewer checking the research-citation AC finds the single highest-value cited rec silently dropped

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the Windows behavior for the `fcntl.flock` advisory lock (e.g. guard the flock behind a POSIX capability check and degrade to git-level retry only on Windows), since `fcntl` is unavailable on the supported Windows platform.
evidence: "serializes the store's index-mutating git invocations across rebar processes with a kernel `fcntl.flock`"
The `fcntl` module does not exist on Windows (CPython ships it only on Unix); `import fcntl` raises ModuleNotFoundError there.
Supported matrix cell: Platform and venue = Windows.
findings.finding: The per-store advisory lock uses `fcntl.flock`, a POSIX-only API unavailable on Windows; the plan names Windows in no fallback path, so the store git write seam cannot import/run on a Windows platform, which is a supported client shape.
findings.location: Approach step 1: "a kernel `fcntl.flock` on a per-store lock file inside the tracker's git dir"
scenarios: Windows platform (developer workstation or CI): any store git write routed through `run_git_write` triggers the `fcntl.flock` path; `import fcntl` / `fcntl.flock` is unavailable, so the caller sees a ModuleNotFoundError/AttributeError crash instead of a git write.
findings.suggested_fix: Gate the `fcntl.flock` advisory lock behind an availability check (try/except ImportError on `fcntl`), and on Windows fall back to relying solely on the git-level jittered retry (step 2), which the plan already states preserves correctness on advisory-lock absence.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the advisory lock's incremental value over the EXISTING lock.py write lock: name the call sites it covers that do NOT already hold `write_lock` (e.g. foreign/non-rebar writers, or read paths), and reconcile the 'JGit in-process fair lock' citation with rebar's per-process CLI model where no intra-process thread contention exists.
evidence: lock.py already provides cross-process serialization: `_acquire_fcntl` does `fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)` and `acquire()`/`write_lock()` wrap it (src/rebar/_store/lock.py:169-189, 528-560).

txn.py's module docstring: 'acquire the unified write lock (rebar._store.lock — fcntl + mkdir dual leg …), … write the append-only event file(s), and git add+commit — releasing the lock only after the commit' — so txn's run_git_write calls run UNDER the existing lock.

event_append routes its index-mutating git ops (`_git_add`, `_git_commit`, `_git_rm`, `_git_commit_paths`) inside `with _lock.write_lock(tracker, dual_window=True)` (src/rebar/_store/event_append.py:415, 527, 377); delete_events likewise (delete.py path routes through run_git_write inside the store write path).

The plan cites JGit's 'in-process fair lock pattern' as the design basis (Approach item 1), but the research it cites (ticket comment 2.2, JGit RefDirectory.java L157-171) describes that lock as serializing 'multiple threads in the SAME process' — an intra-process concern a per-process CLI invocation does not have.

The same research's closing guidance ('IF YOU ARE DESIGNING ON TOP OF THIS') recommends GIT_INDEX_FILE / reducing the contended surface for cross-process/foreign-writer contention, not a second cross-process advisory lock.
findings.finding: The new per-store fcntl.flock advisory lock in run_git_write (Approach item 1) overlaps with the existing cross-process fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX) write lock in lock.py, which the named write call sites already hold; the plan does not state the incremental value the second lock provides.
findings.location: Approach item 1 ("Per-store advisory git-op lock") + Scope: src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py
scenarios: Two rebar processes both doing a txn/claim: both already serialize through lock.py's fcntl+mkdir write lock, so the advisory lock adds a second acquire of the same class of lock for the same effect.

A non-rebar git writer (or a rebar read path not under the write lock) contends on index.lock — the case where the advisory lock could add value, but which the plan neither names nor distinguishes from the already-covered rebar-writer case.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate `src/rebar/_commands/init.py` as a consumer of `run_git_write` and state whether the new advisory-lock serialization + 120s watchdog on init's config/ensure git ops is intended (and covered by tests), or scope the watchdog to exclude it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Account for init.py._git (which also routes through run_git_write): confirm the advisory-lock file path is valid mid-init (git dir may not be fully materialized) and either add init.py to the bounded-call-site inventory or state why it is intentionally excluded.

A reviewer checking AC5 ('each local-only git call site listed in Context is bounded') never audits init.py because it is off-list, yet it now inherits the watchdog

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit prior-art disposition for GIT_INDEX_FILE index-isolation (and Gerrit's retry-the-logical-operation shape) — cite the ticket's own research recommending them, and state why rebar chooses advisory-lock+subprocess-retry instead (or defer isolation to a follow-up with the reason stated).
evidence: Research Part 2: 'The consistent signal across every mature implementation: REDUCE THE CONTENDED SURFACE RATHER THAN CONTEND BETTER. GIT_INDEX_FILE ... eliminates the index-lock class outright'

Research Part 1 footgun 8: 'REBAR DOES NOT USE GIT_INDEX_FILE ISOLATION, AND IT IS THE OBVIOUS FIT ... a dedicated ABSOLUTE-PATH GIT_INDEX_FILE would (a) eliminate index.lock contention with foreign writers outright'

Research names Gerrit's retry-the-LOGICAL-OPERATION (re-reading base state) as 'the battle-tested shape'; the plan retries the same subprocess invocation via _with_index_lock_retry, not the logical op
The Approach cites §1a/§2/§4/§5b for the chosen mechanisms but does not cite or dispose of the index-isolation recommendation the same research foregrounds
findings.finding: The plan's own commissioned OSS research names GIT_INDEX_FILE index-isolation ('reduce the contended surface rather than contend better' — used by git stash, git-filter-branch, and git-annex; git-lfs's absence 'visibly pays') as the ecosystem's dominant answer to index.lock contention, and names Gerrit's 'retry the idempotent logical operation, re-reading base state' as the battle-tested retry shape — yet the Approach adopts only the 'contend-better' branch (advisory lock + retry the SAME subprocess invocation) without explicitly weighing or rejecting index-isolation, so a load-bearing prior-art alternative surfaced by the ticket's own research is left unaddressed.
findings.location: Approach items 1-2 (gitutil advisory lock + _with_index_lock_retry); ticket research comments (Part 1 rec 5b.footgun 8, Part 2 §'IF YOU ARE DESIGNING ON TOP OF THIS')
scenarios: A reviewer or future author asks why rebar contends-better on index.lock instead of removing the contention surface, and the plan has no recorded answer
index.lock contention persists under high concurrency because the retry only rides out conflicts rather than eliminating the shared-index surface the research says is the real fix
findings.suggested_fix: In Approach, add a short 'Alternatives considered' note: acknowledge that the commissioned research ranks GIT_INDEX_FILE isolation (footgun 8 / Part 2 synthesis) as the ecosystem's primary answer and Gerrit's logical-op retry as the battle-tested retry shape; justify choosing the seam-level advisory-lock + same-invocation retry here (e.g. event_append's write path is not the only routed site, isolation is a larger change, ref/config-lock contention is unaffected by a private index) and, if isolation is genuinely superior, scope it as an explicit follow-up ticket rather than leaving it unmentioned.
